arxiv-1812-11549.title: Visibly Pushdown Languages over Sliding Windows
arxiv-1812-11549.creator: Moses Ganardi
arxiv-1812-11549.description: Abstract We investigate the class of visibly pushdown languages in the sliding window model. A sliding window algorithm for a language L L receives a stream of symbols and has to decide at each time step whether the suffix of length n n belongs to L L or not.

arxiv-2012-03958.title: Out of sight, out of mind? The impact of correlated clustering in substructure lensing 2020 Out of sight, out of mind? The impact of correlated clustering in substructure lensing – 14
arxiv-2012-03958.creator: Alexandres Lazar, James S. Bullock, Michael Boylan-Kolchin, Robert Feldmann, Onur Çatmabacak, Leonidas Moustakas
arxiv-2012-03958.description: Abstract A promising route for revealing the existence of dark matter structures on mass scales smaller than the faintest galaxies is through their effect on strong gravitational lenses. We examine the role of local, lens-proximate clustering in boosting the lensing probability relative to contributions from substructure and unclustered line-of-sight (LOS) halos.

arxiv-2104-08241.title: Spatial-Temporal Correlation and Topology Learning for Person Re-Identification in Videos
arxiv-2104-08241.creator: Jiawei Liu, Zheng-Jun Zha *, Wei Wu, Kecheng Zheng, Qibin Sun University of Science and Technology of China, China {jwliu6,zhazj,qibinsun}@ustc.edu.cn, {wuvy,zkcys001}@mail.ustc.edu.cn
arxiv-2104-08241.description: Abstract Video-based person re-identification aims to match pedestrians from video sequences across non-overlapping camera views. The key factor for video person re-identification is to effectively exploit both spatial and temporal clues from video sequences. In this work, we propose a novel Spatial-Temporal Correlation and Topology Learning framework (CTL) to pursue discriminative and robust representation by modeling cross-scale spatial-temporal correlation.

arxiv-2105-08200.title: Photometric Cross-Calibration of the SDSS Stripe 82 Standard Stars catalogue with Gaia EDR3, and Comparison with Pan-STARRS1, DES, CFIS and GALEX catalogues 2021 Photometric Cross-Calibration of the SDSS Stripe 82 Standard Stars catalogue with Gaia EDR3, and Comparison with Pan-STARRS1, DES, CFIS an
arxiv-2105-08200.creator: Karun Thanjavur, Željko Ivezić, Sahar S. Allam Douglas L. Tucker J. Allyn Smith, Stephen Gwyn
arxiv-2105-08200.description: Abstract We extend the SDSS Stripe 82 Standard Stars catalogue with post-2007 SDSS imaging data. This improved version lists averaged SDSS u ​ g ​ r ​ i ​ z ugriz photometry for nearly a million stars brighter than r ∼ 22 r\sim 22 mag. With 2-3 × \times more measurements per star, random errors are 1.4-1.

arxiv-2108-04418.title: Knowledge Enhanced Multi-modal Fake News Detection Conference: ; ; CCS: Computing methodologies Supervised learning by classification CCS: Computing methodologies Neural networks
arxiv-2108-04418.creator: Yi Han, Amila Silva, Ling Luo, Shanika Karunasekera, Christopher Leckie
arxiv-2108-04418.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Yi Han, Amila Silva, Ling Luo, Shanika Karunasekera, Christopher Leckie. Recent years have witnessed the significant damage caused by various types of fake news. Although considerable effort has been applied to address this issue and much progress has been made on detecting fake news, most existing approaches mainly rely on the textual content and/or social context, while knowledge-level information—entities extracted from the news content and the relations between them—is much less explored.

arxiv-2204-04116.creator: Di Wang
arxiv-2204-04116.description: Abstract We point out the C ​ P CP asymmetry in the chain decay of Λ c + → Δ + K ( t ) ( → π + π − ) \Lambda_{c}^{+}\to\Delta^{+}K(t)(\to\pi^{+}\pi^{-}) is determined by the branching fractions of Λ c + → Δ + ⁣ + ​ K − \Lambda^{+}_{c}\to\Delta^{++}K^{-} , Λ c + → Δ + ​

arxiv-2305-07690.title: Tri-hypercharge: a separate gauged weak hypercharge for each fermion family as the origin of flavour
arxiv-2305-07690.creator: Mario Fernández Navarro, and Stephen F. King
arxiv-2305-07690.description: Abstract We propose a tri-hypercharge (TH) embedding of the Standard Model (SM) in which a separate gauged weak hypercharge is associated with each fermion family. In this way, every quark and lepton multiplet carries unique gauge quantum numbers under the extended gauge group, providing the starting point for a theory of flavour.

arxiv-2402-05506.title: Light vector mediators at direct detection experiments
arxiv-2402-05506.creator: Valentina De Romeri, Dimitrios K. Papoulias, Christoph A. Ternes
arxiv-2402-05506.description: Abstract Solar neutrinos induce elastic neutrino-electron scattering in dark matter direct detection experiments, resulting in detectable event rates at current facilities. We analyze recent data from the XENONnT, LUX-ZEPLIN, and PandaX-4T experiments and we derive stringent constraints on several U ​ ( 1 ) ′ U(1)^{\prime} extensions of the Standard Model, accommodating new neutrino-electron interactions.

arxiv-2404-14542.title: UVEB: A Large-scale Benchmark and Baseline Towards Real-World Underwater Video Enhancement
arxiv-2404-14542.creator: Yaofeng Xie Lingwei Kong Kai Chen Ziqiang Zheng Xiao Yu Zhibin Yu Bing Zheng
arxiv-2404-14542.description: Abstract Learning-based underwater image enhancement (UIE) methods have made great progress. However, the lack of large-scale and high-quality paired training samples has become the main bottleneck hindering the development of UIE. The inter-frame information in underwater videos can accelerate or optimize the UIE process.

arxiv-2501-04824.title: Wave induced fracture of a sea ice analog
arxiv-2501-04824.creator: B. Auvity, L. Duchemin, A. Eddi, S. Perrard
arxiv-2501-04824.description: Abstract We study at the laboratory scale the rupture of thin floating sheets made of a brittle material under wave induced mechanical forcing. We show that the rupture occurs where the curvature is maximum, and the break up threshold strongly depends on the wave properties.

arxiv-2502-18699.title: MPO: An Efficient Post-Processing Framework for Mixing Diverse Preference Alignment
arxiv-2502-18699.creator: Tianze Wang, Dongnan Gui, Yifan Hu, Shuhang Lin, Linjun Zhang
arxiv-2502-18699.description: Abstract Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) has shown promise in aligning large language models (LLMs). Yet its reliance on a singular reward model often overlooks the diversity of human preferences. Recent approaches address this limitation by leveraging multi-dimensional feedback to fine-tune corresponding reward models and train LLMs using reinforcement learning.

arxiv-2504-16589.title: More on genuine multi-entropy and holography
arxiv-2504-16589.creator: Norihiro Iizuka, Simon Lin, and Mitsuhiro Nishida
arxiv-2504-16589.description: Abstract By generalizing the construction of genuine multi-entropy GM ( 𝚚 ) {\rm GM}^{\mathtt{(q)}} for genuine multi-partite entanglement proposed in the previous paper [ 1 ] , we give a prescription on how to construct GM ( 𝚚 ) {\rm GM}^{\mathtt{(q)}} systematically for any 𝚚 \mathtt{q} .

arxiv-2505-14388.title: Algorithmic Hiring and Diversity: Reducing Human-Algorithm Similarity for Better Outcomes
arxiv-2505-14388.creator: Prasanna Parasurama, Panos Ipeirotis
arxiv-2505-14388.description: Abstract Algorithmic tools are increasingly used in hiring to improve fairness and diversity, often by enforcing constraints such as gender-balanced candidate shortlists. However, we show theoretically and empirically that enforcing equal representation at the shortlist stage does not necessarily translate into more diverse final hires, even when there is no gender bias in the hiring stage.

arxiv-2508-15830.title: DAIQ: Auditing Demographic Attribute Inference from Question in LLMs
arxiv-2508-15830.creator: Srikant Panda, Hitesh Laxmichand Patel, Shahad Al-Khalifa, Amit Agarwal, Hend Al-Khalifa, Sharefah Al-Ghamdi
arxiv-2508-15830.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) are known to reflect social biases when demographic attributes, such as gender or race, are explicitly present in the input. But even in their absence, these models still infer user identities based solely on question phrasing.

arxiv-2509-04172.title: Welschinger–Witt invariants
arxiv-2509-04172.creator: Erwan Brugallé, Johannes Rau, Kirsten Wickelgren
arxiv-2509-04172.description: Abstract . Welschinger invariants are signed counts of real rational curves satisfying contraints. Quadratic Gromov–Witten invariants give such counts over general fields of characteristic different from 2 and 3. For rational del Pezzo surfaces over a field, we propose a conjectural relationship between Welschinger and quadratic Gromov–Witten invariants.

arxiv-2602-20332.title: No One Size Fits All: QueryBandits for LLM Hallucination Mitigation
arxiv-2602-20332.creator: Nicole Cho, William Watson, Alec Koppel, Sumitra Ganesh, Manuela Veloso
arxiv-2602-20332.description: Abstract Advanced reasoning capabilities in Large Language Models (LLMs) have led to more frequent hallucinations; yet most mitigation work focuses on open-source models for post-hoc detection and parameter editing. The dearth of studies focusing on hallucinations in closed-source models is especially concerning, as they constitute the vast majority of models in institutional deployments.

pmc-10532668.title: Effects of TiC, Si, and Al on Combustion Synthesis of Ti3SiC2/TiC/Ti5Si3 Composites
pmc-10532668.creator: Chun-Liang Yeh, Kuan-Ling Lai
pmc-10532668.description: The fabrication of Ti3SiC2 from TiC-containing reactant compacts was investigated by combustion synthesis in the mode of self-propagating high-temperature synthesis (SHS). The initial sample composition was formulated based on (3 − x)Ti + ySi + (2 − x)C + xTiC + zAl, with stoichiometric parameters of x from 0 to 0.7, y = 1.0 and 1.

pmc-10559601.title: Real-world evidence with a retrospective cohort of 15,968 COVID-19 hospitalized patients suggests 21 new effective treatments
pmc-10559601.creator: Carlos Loucera, Rosario Carmona, Marina Esteban-Medina, Gerrit Bostelmann, Dolores Muñoyerro-Muñiz, Román Villegas, María Peña-Chilet, Joaquín Dopazo
pmc-10559601.description: PurposeDespite the extensive vaccination campaigns in many countries, COVID-19 is still a major worldwide health problem because of its associated morbidity and mortality. Therefore, finding efficient treatments as fast as possible is a pressing need. Drug repurposing constitutes a convenient alternative when the need for new drugs in an unexpected medical scenario is urgent, as is the case with COVID-19.

pmc-11578366.title: Solar‐Driven Evaporator With “Starburst Turbine” Design Featuring Directional Salt Crystallization, Antibacterial, and Catalytic Multifunctionality for Efficient Water Purification
pmc-11578366.creator: Jiahui Yu, Lele Li, Yuxuan Liu, Jie Wen, Shu Liu, Jiye Li, Junyi Ning, Changxiang Shao, Tao Wu, Bing Liu
pmc-11578366.description: Facing the global challenge of water scarcity, solar‐driven desalination is considered a sustainable technology for obtaining freshwater from seawater. However, issues such as uncontrolled salt crystallization and bacterial contamination limit its efficiency and practicality. This study proposes an innovative solar‐driven evaporator designed to address these challenges using optimized shape design and advanced photothermal materials.

pmc-11697562.title: Targeted macrophage mannose receptor (CD206)-specific protein delivery via engineered extracellular vesicles
pmc-11697562.creator: Leyla A Ovchinnikova, Daria Y Tanygina, Samir S Dzhelad, Evgeniy G Evtushenko, Dmitriy V Bagrov, Alexander G Gabibov, Yakov A Lomakin
pmc-11697562.description: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) show great potential for therapeutic delivery to human cells, with a focus on modulating immune responses. The most promising targets for inducing humoral and cellular immunity against a specific antigen are macrophages (Mϕs) and dendritic cells (DCs).

pmc-12382047.title: Integrated analysis of 16 S endophytic bacteria and non-targeted metabolomics reveals the drought response mechanisms of Portulaca Oleracea L
pmc-12382047.creator: Xinyu Zhao, Luxiang Liang, Shi Qi, Jiahui Fang, Ping Li, Mengyun Xu, Jian Yan
pmc-12382047.description: BackgroundDrought is currently one of the biggest challenges facing global agricultural production. Purslane (Portulaca oleracea L.) has attracted widespread attention due to its exceptional drought resistance. However, the dynamics in endophytic bacterial communities and their synergistic response mechanisms with metabolites under drought stress in purslane remain poorly understood.

pmc-12410764.title: Reaching a cell monolayer at the end of hiPSC differentiation enhances neural crest lineage commitment
pmc-12410764.creator: Filipa M. Duarte, Jeroen van de Peppel, Irene M.J. Mathijssen, Johan W. van Neck, Michael Klymkowsky, Michael Klymkowsky, Michael Klymkowsky
pmc-12410764.description: Neural crest stem cells (NCSCs) compose a highly migratory, multipotent, stem cell population arising from the neural plate border of the embryonic ectoderm. Investigating the development of NCSCs is critical in understanding both embryonic development and abnormal events that underlie neurocristopathies.

pmc-12535591.title: Trends in non-animal scaffolds for cultured meat structuration
pmc-12535591.creator: Gabrielle Antunes Seibert, Vivian Feddern, Ana Paula Almeida Bastos, Anuj Kumar, Silvani Verruck
pmc-12535591.description: Cultured meat offers a sustainable protein alternative to meet growing food demands, relying on scaffolds to structure muscle tissue. This review evaluates plant-derived and polymeric scaffolds—synthetic polymers, peptides, fungal/plant materials—and techniques like 3D bioprinting, electrospinning, and microcarriers. Scaffold types (fibrous, porous, hydrogels) are assessed for adhesion, degradation, cost, and scalability.

pmc-12651963.title: Complete Mitochondrial Genome and Phylogenetic Analysis of Turdus pallidus (Passeriformes, Turdidae)
pmc-12651963.creator: Qingbin Zhan, Yin Tang, Xiaoyan Zhao, Xiaoming Xue, Yunxia Chen, Yalin Huang, Zissis Mamuris
pmc-12651963.description: Background: Thrushes (family Turdidae) are ecologically important passerine birds widely distributed across the Northern Hemisphere. However, the phylogenetic placement of several East Asian congeners, including Turdus pallidus, remains insufficiently resolved due to the limited resolution of partial mitochondrial or nuclear markers used in previous studies. Methods: In this work, we sequenced and annotated the complete mitochondrial genome of T.

pmc-12750307.title: Chemoradioimmunotherapy versus chemoimmunotherapy or chemoradiotherapy in extensive‐stage small‐cell lung cancer: A retrospective analysis of survival outcomes
pmc-12750307.creator: Jinmin Han, Ying Hua, Xue Wu, Xiufeng Tang, Chengxin Liu
pmc-12750307.description: Background and purposeCurrent evidence is insufficient to define the value of thoracic radiotherapy (TRT) following chemoimmunotherapy (CT‐IO) in extensive‐stage small‐cell lung cancer (ES‐SCLC). We aimed to ascertain whether incorporating immunotherapy (IO) could improve survival and explore the efficacy of TRT in combination with CT‐IO among patients with ES‐SCLC.MethodsClinical data were retrospectively analyzed.

pmc-12998244.title: Roar Data: Redefining a Lion's Roar Using Machine Learning
pmc-12998244.creator: Jonathan Growcott, Alex Lobora, Andrew Markham, Charlotte E Searle, Johan Wahlström, Matthew Wijers, Benno I Simmons
pmc-12998244.description: For territorial advertisement and intra‐pride communication African lions emit a roaring bout, of which one component, is their iconic roar. The full‐throated roar of a lion has recently been shown to be a unique and individually identifiable signature. At the same time, the frequency of large‐scale passive acoustic monitoring surveys has increased.

pmc-13207279.title: The Effective Biodegradation of Poly(ε-caprolactone) by Engineered Yeast Yarrowia lipolytica Producing Lipase B
pmc-13207279.creator: Żaneta Zdanowska, Lara Serrano-Aguirre, Aneta Krystyna Urbanek, Adam Dobrowolski, Aleksandra M. Mirończuk
pmc-13207279.description: Poly(ε-caprolactone) (PCL) is a biodegradable aliphatic polyester with applications in many areas. Lipase B from Moesziomyces antarcticus (CALB, previously known as Candida antarctica lipase B) is a well-characterize enzyme capable of hydrolysing several polyesters. In this study, the codon-optimized gene encoding CALB was cloned into the yeast Yarrowia lipolytica to enhance its natural capabilities toward polyesters biodegradation.
